text:
Neither starter is playing. Dennis Hildeby gets the net for Tampa Bay over Andrei Vasilevskiy, who has 12 of the Lightning's 15 starts, and Calvin Pickard starts for Minnesota over Jesper Wallstedt, who has 16 of 18. Pickard has stopped .833 in two games. Hildeby is at -0.2 goals saved above expected this season after +10.1 in 20 games last year. Put two teams that generate this many chances in front of those two, and you get our numbers' projection: 3.25 goals for Tampa, 3.19 for Minnesota.

The Wild come in on the second night of a back-to-back, after a 4-1 win over San Jose that made it three straight. They've outscored teams 13-4 in that run, though the chances only half back it (52% of the expected goals, with the goaltending saving 4.7 above expected). Kirill Kaprizov scored his league-leading 16th goal last night and has points in seven straight. "Can't say it enough, I just feel like we can tilt the ice when they're out there," Quinn Hughes said of the Kaprizov, Matt Boldy and Joel Eriksson Ek line, per NHL.com's Heather Rule. All three are on seven-game point streaks. Minnesota is without both Folignos and Jared Spurgeon.

Tampa has points in five straight (3-0-2). Brayden Point is one point from 700 for his career and has points in six straight. Brandon Hagel, named NHL.com's Bolts best player of the month, is our likeliest Lightning scorer at 39%, and Nikita Kucherov is 81% for a point.

Both teams tilt the ice at five on five (55% of the expected goals for Tampa, 54% for Minnesota). The Lightning won the first meeting 3-2 on Oct 8, a game they deserved 57% of the time.
headline: Two backups, two hot teams, one coin flip

hunch.text: Two backups behind two teams that create this much: our gut says the projection undersells it and this one clears seven goals.
